Web design in Dallas, TX, from someone who shows the work first

If you are shopping for web design in Dallas, TX, you have probably noticed how many companies want your business. Search the phrase and you get page after page of agencies, freelancers and builders, each with a slick portfolio and a quote that only arrives after a discovery call. Choosing between them is hard because you are being asked to pay for something you have not seen.

Dominion Web Design Pro skips that step. Maurice Johnson builds a demo of your website first, using your business name and trade. You open it, pass it around, and only then decide whether to buy. When you do, every page on the finished site is written by hand for your business and the parts of Dallas you serve.

The business itself is in Big Sandy, East Texas, east of the Metroplex. Nothing about the work depends on being down the street from you.

A city of distinct districts, and customers who search by them

Dallas is about 1.3 million people inside the city limits, according to the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, and it does not behave like one market. Deep Ellum, east of downtown, is known for live music, bars and late-night food. Lower Greenville is a strip of restaurants and patios. Across the Trinity River in Oak Cliff, the Bishop Arts District is built around independently owned shops, galleries and cafes. Each of those places draws a different customer, and each is searched by name.

Language matters here too. Census estimates for 2019 to 2023 show 41.1 percent of Dallas residents five and up speak something other than English at home, nearly double the national rate. For a contractor, a clinic or a restaurant, that is a real question about who reads your site and how they decide to call.

The rest of the Dallas small business picture is what you would expect from a big service economy: trades and home services across the older neighborhoods and the suburbs, professional offices downtown and along the freeways, food businesses everywhere. What they share online is competition. A Dallas business needs pages that say exactly what it does and exactly where, or it gets lost behind the firms that do.

Why the exact words matter in Dallas search

The keyword data pulled for this site shows how sharply phrasing changes the field. "Web design in Dallas TX" gets about 5,400 searches a month with a low difficulty score of 13, while "web design in Dallas" gets about 4,400 with a difficulty of 68. "Website design agency Dallas" sits at about 590 searches with a difficulty of 7. Same city, same service, very different competition depending on a couple of words.

Your customers do the same with your trade. A homeowner might type "foundation repair Dallas," "foundation repair Lake Highlands" or "foundation repair near me," and each one is a slightly different contest. A good Dallas website does not chase every variation; it covers the services and places you really serve, in plain words, so the right searches have a page to find.

Before you sign with any Dallas web design company

Dallas owners who have been through a bad website project tend to describe the same few problems. Here is how to spot them before you pay, whoever you hire.

  • The site lives on their platform. If the agency's account holds your domain or your files, leaving can mean starting over. Ask who owns what, in writing.
  • The price grows after launch. A low build fee with a large monthly retainer can cost more in two years than a one-time build. Ask for the total for the first two years.
  • The pages are copies. Ask to see a city page from a site they built. If it reads like every other city page with the name swapped, yours will too.
  • Nobody answers after the sale. Ask who handles a change request and how fast. Here, it is Maurice, by phone or email.

Get the answers by email, not just on a call, so you can compare companies side by side later.

A good company will answer all four without hesitation. If the answers are vague, keep looking, and that includes looking at us.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Dallas. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

What remote delivery means in practice: you text or email photos and details, Maurice builds and writes, and you review every page by link before it goes live. If you would rather have a designer you can meet for coffee in Uptown, a Dallas firm can do that, and it is a fair reason to choose one.

Free help for small businesses in Dallas

Independent of anything to do with us, these are good first calls for a Dallas owner.

City of Dallas Small Business Center

Set up by the city in 2021 to bring its business diversity, workforce and entrepreneurship programs under one roof, including advising and funding programs for small businesses.

North Texas SBDC

The Small Business Development Center network hosted by Dallas College offers no-cost advising and free or low-cost workshops for businesses across North Texas.

Dallas Regional Chamber

Founded in 1909, one of the oldest chambers of commerce in the country, focused on business advocacy and regional growth.

Common questions

How do I choose a website design company in Dallas?

Ask each one the same questions: Can I see something built for my business before I pay? Who owns the domain and the files? What is the full monthly cost after launch? Who will I actually talk to? Compare the answers side by side. Dominion's are: a free demo first, you own everything, a one-time price for the site, and you talk to Maurice, the person who builds it.

What does a website design agency in Dallas charge?

Dallas pricing ranges widely, from do-it-yourself builders at a few dollars a month to agency builds that cost thousands plus a monthly retainer. Dominion keeps it simple for Dallas owners: a $497 Starter build, a $997 Pro build or a $1,997 Agency build, each a single payment. Ongoing site care costs $49 monthly, and it is folded into the AI agent plan if you choose to keep that. For how the wider market prices this work, see the website designer cost guide.

Are you a Dallas web design company?

No, and this page will not pretend otherwise. Dominion Web Design Pro is based in Big Sandy, East Texas, and builds sites for Dallas businesses remotely. Everything happens by link, phone and email, and the prices are the same as for any other city.

Can my Dallas website have pages for Oak Cliff, Lake Highlands or the suburbs?

Yes, if you get work there. Pro includes 10 city pages, and in Dallas those can be neighborhoods and nearby cities such as Garland, Irving, Richardson, Mesquite or Grand Prairie. Each page is researched and written for that place, not copied with the name swapped.

How long does it take to get a Dallas small business website live?

Expect a Starter build online one to two weeks after you hand over details. Agency builds roll out in batches, and the opening batch is up within fourteen days. The thing that slows most projects is waiting on photos and details, so gather those early.
